name: Igal
title: The Spy from the Tribe of Issachar
summary: Igal, son of Joseph, was one of the twelve spies that Moses sent into the land of Canaan to explore it. He represented the tribe of Issachar. Igal was among the ten spies who returned with a negative report and discouraged the Israelites from entering the land.

keyEvents.title: Chosen as a Scout
keyEvents.description: Jigal, son of Joseph, was chosen by Moses to represent the tribe of Issachar as one of the twelve scouts sent to explore the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Sent to the Land of Canaan
keyEvents.description: Moses sent the twelve scouts, including Jigal, from the wilderness of Paran to explore the land of Canaan and bring back information about its people and terrain.

keyEvents.title: Exploring the Land
keyEvents.description: Jigal and the other scouts explored the land of Canaan for forty days, from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob near Lebo-Hamat.

keyEvents.title: The Negative Report
keyEvents.description: Jigal was among the ten scouts who gave a negative report about the land. They claimed that the people of Canaan were too strong and that the Israelites could not take possession of it.

keyEvents.title: The People's Rebellion
keyEvents.description: The negative report from Jigal and the other scouts caused the entire congregation of Israel to weep and complain against Moses and Aaron, wishing to return to Egypt.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on the Scouts
keyEvents.description: As punishment for their false and discouraging report, Jigal and the other nine unfaithful scouts were struck down by a plague and died in the presence of the Lord. Only Joshua and Caleb survived.
